claims.assertion: The fare was quoted at $10.02 on a 1× multiplier when the rider booked, and the quote is binding at the multiplier in effect at quote time; the charged fare of $11.88 was billed at 1.3×, so the rider paid $1.86 above the binding quote.

The in-app notice at 14:10:20 (before the 14:13 trip start) reads in full: "Fares are 1.3× higher right now. Your new estimated fare is $12.65. You can cancel for free." — it does state the new multiplier, a revised estimated fare and free cancellation, so under the clause as written this element is met and, on the notice point alone, the higher fare may stand.

The revised estimate of $12.65 in the notice is $0.77 above the $11.88 the rider was actually charged, so the notice quoted a fare that does not match the amount billed; the rider's complaint that the notice was misleading on this point is factually accurate even though a stated estimate need not be identical to the final fare.

There is no route deviation to attribute the increase to: the actual distance of 2.4 km is 0.1 km shorter than the 2.5 km optimal route and the trip took 3.2 min against an estimated 5.1 min, so the whole $1.86 excess over the quote comes from the surge multiplier change.

The surge differential is (1.3 − 1) × the surgeable subtotal of $8.18 = $2.45, capped at the $1.86 by which the fare exceeds the quote, and the $1.25 booking fee is surge-exempt and not part of any refund.

The complete, fully timestamped chat contains only the rider's pickup note and the driver's ETA reply, and the driver's statement is that he simply drove the route the app showed; nothing in the record shows the rider agreeing to any reroute or extra charge.

The rider has held the account 1290 days with a 4.6 rating and zero upheld disputes in 90 days, so credibility supports resolving this fare issue in the rider's favour; the driver's own single upheld dispute is not a repeat pattern and no flag is requested against him here.

weaknesses: The platform's surge log (F9) shows a notice was sent in-app at 14:10:20, before trip start, containing the new multiplier, a revised estimated fare and free cancellation — so on the wording of SURGE-1 the notice element is arguably met and no surge refund is owed (SURGE-2 row 1, no_action).

The notice was sent only ~2 minutes before pickup (F9 vs the 14:13 trip start), and the revised estimate of $12.65 (F9) exceeds the $11.88 actually charged (F5), so my 'misleading notice' argument (C3) is a mismatch complaint, not a missing-notice complaint; the clause only requires a stated estimate.
The excess over the quote is small ($1.86, F8) and the disputed amount is under $10, so TH-1 makes a system ruling final and the practical upside is limited.
